findings.title: zip(error_ids, events.values()) misaligns error IDs with event data when some events are missing
findings.body: In fetch_error_details, `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` returns a dict that only contains entries for node_ids that were found. If some events are missing from nodestore, `events.values()` will have fewer items than `error_ids`, and `zip(error_ids, events.values())` will pair the wrong error_id with the wrong event data. For example, if error_ids=[A,B,C] but only A and C are found, zip will pair A with A's data and B with C's data. The fix should iterate over error_ids and look up each node_id individually in the events dict, e.g., `for event_id in error_ids: data = events.get(Event.generate_node_id(project_id, event_id=event_id))`.

findings.title: Mutual exclusion validation for age/timestamp uses truthiness instead of key presence
findings.body: In validate_timestamp, the check `if self.initial_data.get("age")` will be falsy when age=0, which is a valid value. Similarly in validate_age, `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp")` will be falsy when timestamp=0. This means a report with both age=0 and timestamp=5 will pass validation when it should be rejected. The checks should use `"age" in self.initial_data` and `"timestamp" in self.initial_data` respectively.

findings.title: Feature-flagged TableWidgetVisualization renders empty table with no actual data
findings.body: When the `use-table-widget-visualization` feature flag is enabled, the code renders a TableWidgetVisualization with hardcoded empty data (`columns={[]}`, `tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}}`) instead of passing the actual `result.data`, `result.meta`, and column information. This means enabling this feature flag will cause all dashboard table widgets to display empty tables, losing all data visibility. The actual table results (fields, data, meta, etc.) need to be wired through to the new component.

findings.title: Full request body logged at INFO level on unauthenticated endpoint
findings.body: The endpoint logs `logger.info("browser_report_received", extra={"request_body": request.data})` for every request. Since this is an unauthenticated endpoint (permission_classes=()) that receives browser Reporting API data, this will log URLs, user agents, and potentially sensitive report bodies (CSP violations can contain page content details) at INFO level in production logs. This creates a privacy concern and could lead to log volume issues. Consider logging at DEBUG level or only logging metadata (report type, count) rather than full bodies.

findings.title: analytics.record with request.user.id may fail for org auth token authentication
findings.body: The analytics.record call uses `user_id=request.user.id` unconditionally. While the analytics event defines user_id as `required=False`, the code always attempts to access `request.user.id`. If the request is authenticated via an org auth token where `request.user` might be an AnonymousUser or a token-based identity without a traditional `.id`, this will raise an AttributeError and fail the entire request before any processing occurs. The code later checks `is_org_auth_token_auth(request.auth)` suggesting token auth is supported. Consider using `getattr(request.user, 'id', None)` or recording analytics after determining the user identity.

findings.title: get_merged_pr_single_issue_template references PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title which may not exist on that class
findings.body: The static method `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` on `CommitContextIntegration` calls `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title)`, but `_truncate_title` is defined as a static method on `CommitContextIntegration` itself (line 577). If `PRCommentWorkflow` does not inherit from `CommitContextIntegration`, this will raise AttributeError at runtime when generating PR comments. The call should likely be `CommitContextIntegration._truncate_title(title)` or the method reference should be verified against the actual class hierarchy.
